📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il tifo organizzato conferma la presenza il 6 dicembre e precisano che non sarà un rientro definitivo.

Così il Tifo Organizzato, tramite un comunicato pubblicato sull'account Instagram.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

A dicembre abbiamo deciso di regalarci un mese intero di Lazio.

Un anno fa questa sarebbe stata la normalità per il popolo bianco celeste ma purtroppo, un presidente tiranno e la sua pletora di tifosi giallorossi, ci hanno costretto a quell’estremo atto di amore che ci ha portato lontano da casa nostra.

In questi lunghi mesi di lontananza abbiamo capito quanto il consenso di questa protesta poggi su basi molto solide perchè ha continuato ad avere dalla sua parte un popolo che ha liberamente scelto di appoggiarla, di contro i vertici di questa società non hanno fatto assolutamente nulla per riavvicinare la tifoseria continuando ad andare nella direzione esattamente opposta ed il popolo laziale ha continuato a scegliere da che parte stare.

Poche eccezioni si sono distinte, tra tutti sicuramente ci sono mister Gattuso, che più volte ha ribadito di capire ed accettare la nostra decisione esprimendo però il “sogno” di vedere lo Stadio Olimpico pieno della sua gente, e la sua squadra (plasmata ad immagine e somiglianza del mister) che ad ogni trasferta è venuta sotto il settore ospite a prendersi il meritato applauso e sappiamo che ci sono vicini!

Per lui, per la squadra, ma soprattutto per tutti quei bambini e tifosi che hanno aderito alla protesta allontanandosi dallo stadio, a quelli che non sono riusciti ad acquistare il biglietto per il derby ed a tutti i laziali che soffrono lontano dalla propria amata Lazio, abbiamo deciso rendere omaggio entrando il 6 dicembre alla partita Lazio-Atalanta.

Caricheremo così anche i ragazzi prima della stracittadina dando un assaggio dell’ambiente che troveranno il 13 dicembre, dimostrando di essere sempre al loro fianco, perché se lo meritano!

Negli scorsi anni siamo andati ad incitarli a Formello ma ormai quel centro sportivo non lo sentiamo più “casa nostra”, sono state fatte molte amichevoli ed il signor Lotito ha pensato bene di farle a porte chiuse per paura della contestazione, ha fatto chiudere la squadra dentro un bunker fregandosene di tutti quei tifosi che avrebbero voluto vedere ed incitare quei ragazzi che oggi ci stanno regalando grandi soddisfazioni.

Non ne facciamo una questione economica, la sortita del pack scontato per tre partite non ha avuto gli effetti desiderati dall’ufficio marketing, la nostra passione non si compra con gli sconti, la nostra fede non è un prodotto da supermercato, scegliamo noi quando entrare, riprovateci ...sarete più fortunati!

Questo non vuol dire bloccare la contestazione, che per questa partita continuerà dentro lo stadio, o erroneamente pensare che si rientri definitivamente, e’ solo l’ennesima prova di unità e compattezza di un popolo contro un despota.

La protesta proseguirà con le stesse modalità di inizio anno, si continuerà a presenziare solo in trasferta ed ai derby e poi, se e quando lo vogliamo tutti noi, sceglieremo (forse) qualche altra giornata di lazialità.

Non si tratta di un passo indietro, altri lo debbono fare, ad iniziare dal tifoso romanista che occupa la sedia del responsabile della comunicazione (al derby come si comporterà!? Tiferà con cuore o continuerà a pensare al portafogli?) noi restiamo fermi sulle nostre posizioni che restano le stesse e non sono minimamente condizionate dall’ottima partenza e dalla meritata posizione in classifica.

Il nostro giudizio completamente negativo su comportamenti del signor Lotito, della gestione vergognosa ed approssimativa della prima società della Capitale, ci fanno restare fermi nella convinzione che un cambio sia urgente per stare al passo con quel mondo del calcio che viaggia ad una velocità tripla rispetto alla nostra Lazio, è doveroso nei confronti di un popolo che vive quotidianamente questo immenso amore e che invece si trova costretto a vivere in un incubo fatto di pressappochismo e botte di fortuna.

Industry observers note that come già detto quando abbiamo deciso di non abbonarci e di seguire la Lazio solo in trasferta, anche questa volta chi vuole restare fuori è libero di farlo, chi invece vuole seguirci si prepari a vivere con noi 90 minuti di puro amore! Portate i bambini, mettetegli una bandiera in mano ed una sciarpa al collo e ditegli che per Natale ci regaliamo tutti un dicembre da laziali con quattro partite che ci riossigeneranno fino al derby di ritorno!

Durante la puntata di Elastici, l’ex portiere Viviano ha parlato del pareggio rocambolesco dell’Inter in casa dell’Atalanta e dell’atteggiamento dei nerazzurri:.

“Per me è discretamente inaccettabile. Non è una questione di errori individuali, che ci sono stati, non è una questione di condizione fisica, che sicuramente è precaria, quella di Curtis Jones piuttosto che di Lautaro. È una questione di consegnarsi all'Atalanta e abbassarsi in quella maniera, soprattutto vedendo che ogni volta che vai avanti vai in porta. Giochi contro il Manchester City, stasera a Napoli, a un certo punto ti abbassi per forza, ti ci portano ad abbassarti. Va bene, lo capisco, ma non era quella la partita”.

“L’Atalanta ha tentato il tutto per tutto, ha dei meriti e l'Inter si è consegnata. Thuram che viene a fare il quinto di centrocampo, Curtis Jones che passeggiava per il campo, Lautaro non in condizione. Ma c'era proprio un'idea che secondo me è sbagliata di base. Sembrava il gatto col topo? In vantaggio di due, adesso ci addormentiamo. Due, andiamo in vantaggio un'altra volta, adesso ci addormentiamo. E non è bastato.

Recent findings suggest that “Staccare la spina, secondo me, oggi è proprio quella cosa che, per varie ragioni, compresa quella regolamentare, non funziona più. Io l'ho fatto per una vita, cioè ho giocato in squadre che lo facevano: vinciamo, troviamo tutti i mezzi possibili, palla fuori dalla tribuna, quello rimane in terra, perdiamo tempo, la portiamo alla bandierina, ci abbassiamo, siamo tutti in area. Oggi non si può fare perché ti portano tanti giocatori in area, perché non c'è più modo di perdere tempo, perché è tutto veloce. Quindi, se il calcio ti sta dimostrando continuamente che non si può fare, non lo fare.

A posteriori qualche critica a Chivu gliela fai: si fa male Calhanoglu e toglie Barella e Mkhitaryan. Secondo me uno dei tre ci deve essere in campo perché Sucic ti può piacere o no, ma è tatticamente indisciplinato, Curtis Jones non te lo dico nemmeno, Stankovic è un ragazzo giovane. Akanji indisciplinato nelle letture, secondo me anche l’allenatore l’ha un po’ sottovalutata Secondo me fare entrare Stankovic che arrivava da un mezzo infortunio, Jones che non gioca da due mesi, Lautaro che veniva da un infortunio è stato un po’ come dire: va beh la portiamo a casa lo stesso”.

Tre punti consentirebbero alla squadra di Chivu di scavalcare proprio i tedeschi che hanno un punto in più, e conservare una piccola speranza di accedere agli ottavi senza passare dai playoff.

Industry observers note that "Lo Stoccarda oggi. Il Borussia Dortmund alla prossima, il 9 dicembre. La Champions dell’Inter diventa una mini Bundesliga, contro due avversarie che la precedono in classifica. E che quindi banalmente vanno battute e scavalcate per cercare l’aggancio complicatissimo, ma non ancora impossibile, alla top 8. It has been revealed that arsenal have played six Premier League games this season and Bruno Guimarães has been a match-winning force in two of them. At this rate, he might justify his enormous £75m transfer fee by Christmas.

The Brazilian was not signed to be Arsenal’s super sub but that is the role he appears to be playing in these early days in north London. Against Leeds United here, as it was against Sunderland last month, he came off the bench when the champions were struggling. And as it was at Sunderland, he produced a thumping finish to put Arsenal on their way to three points.

This is the value of signing a 28-year-old with significant Premier League experience. As Arsenal laboured against an impressively organised and courageous Leeds side, Mikel Arteta knew that Guimarães was capable of coming into the game and adjusting to its demands. There has been no adaptation period required for Guimarães, who is fast becoming one of the most popular players in north London.

According to recent reports, the finish, which put Arsenal 2-1 ahead at the Emirates Stadium, marked an emphatic conclusion to a fabulous passing sequence. Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard and Declan Rice all combined at speed before Guimarães charged on to Rice’s flick. “It was a beauty,” said Arteta of the goal. The move had actually begun at the feet of Guimarães a few moments earlier, when he nutmegged an opponent in style.

The winning goal came just eight minutes after Riccardo Calafiori, Arsenal’s thrilling left-back/centre-forward hybrid, had pulled them level in the game. James Justin had struck for Leeds shortly after half-time, creating a horrible anxiety among the home fans here, and for much of the afternoon Daniel Farke’s side were the better team.

Leeds, though, could not compete with Arsenal for depth. The arrival of Guimarães as a 63rd-minute substitute represented a flexing of Arteta’s managerial muscle, in his first match since signing a new long-term contract, and the Brazilian offered a moment of attacking quality that his opponents were unable to replicate.

It was actually the first competitive home game that Guimarães had played for Arsenal since his transfer from Newcastle United, as a result of a few niggles and the club’s unusual run of four consecutive away matches before the international break. The most recent of those was the 3-0 thrashing by Brighton, which was one of their worst defeats of the last few seasons.

This gritty victory represented a necessary response to that defeat, even if the performance was far from dominant. “We had a point to prove,” mentioned Arteta. “Something was touched in our identity against Brighton.”.

Sources indicate that guimarães, too, clearly felt that some wrongs needed to be made right. For all his brilliance in this game and against Sunderland, he had produced a horrible showing at the Amex Stadium a few weeks ago. “He was not at that level against Brighton,” noted Arteta. “This is the level for Arsenal. Every week, every game, every minute, every action you have to be at that level. At Brighton, he wasn’t. Today, he was much better.”.

It has been revealed that leeds had not lost in their opening five Premier League matches of this season and it was easy to see why. They were willing to press Arsenal high up the pitch, taking risks and engaging in physical duels, and the strategy proved hugely effective for an hour.

It has been revealed that if they had been more precise in the final third, they could have been a few goals ahead by the time Justin converted Gabriel Gudmundsson’s left-wing cross after 55 minutes. Anton Stach, who was accidentally blocked by team-mate Jayden Bogle, and Gudmundsson both went close in the first half.

Three weeks on from the fifth round of Premier League fixtures in which the champions Arsenal were beaten 3-0 by Brighton and todays’ visitors, Leeds United, who remain unbeaten, drew in a tepid goalless fixture with Crystal Palace, we finally get to the sixth. L’ex centrocampista della Lazio si allena già con il pallone e, dopo l’intervento, vuole tornare al cento per cento.

Matias Vecino si prepara a tornare in campo dopo l’intervento e alcuni mesi lontano dal calcio giocato. L’ex centrocampista di Lazio e Inter, che ha risolto il contratto con il Celta Vigo, racconta di stare recuperando e indica metà dicembre come il momento in cui conta di essere pronto. A Gianlucadimarzio.com ha detto: «Sto bene, sto recuperando. Mi sto preparando per il ritorno in campo».

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Vecino ha ricordato le difficoltà incontrate all’inizio del percorso. Pur sapendo che l’operazione sarebbe stata abbastanza semplice, era consapevole che il recupero avrebbe richiesto tempo: «All'inizio è stato un po' più difficile, affrontare un intervento non è mai semplice. Sapevo che si trattava di un'operazione abbastanza semplice, ma che sarebbero serviti un paio di mesi per recuperare».

Industry observers note that il centrocampista è tornato a Roma con la famiglia e prosegue il lavoro insieme al suo staff. «Siamo tornati a Roma con la mia famiglia, sto facendo un bel lavoro con il mio staff. Mi sto preparando», ha spiegato. Il suo obiettivo resta riprendere a giocare, seguendo passo dopo passo il percorso di recupero.

Il classe ’91 ha indicato anche quando pensa di poter essere pronto: «Per metà dicembre sarò pronto. Sono molto ansioso di tornare, sto già lavorando sul campo con il pallone e tutto procede per il verso giusto. Poi vedremo quali opportunità potranno presentarsi».

Una volta recuperata la condizione, Vecino vorrebbe tornare in Serie A. Conosce il campionato italiano, nel quale ha giocato con Inter e Lazio, ma non intende limitare la scelta a questa possibilità. Negli ultimi mesi della scorsa stagione ha vestito la maglia del Celta Vigo.

According to recent reports, «Sarebbe bello tornare in Serie A perché è un campionato che conosco e nel quale mi conoscono. Vedremo quello che succederà», ha dichiarato. Ha poi aggiunto: «Sono aperto anche ad altre opzioni. Dipende dalle possibilità che capiteranno».

Prima di valutare le occasioni che si presenteranno, il centrocampista vuole completare il recupero: «L'importante è stare bene, continuare a recuperare e tornare al cento per cento. Mi manca poco per raggiungere la migliore condizione, poi vedremo». La voglia di rimettersi in gioco passa dunque dal ritorno alla piena forma.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 02:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.

As the fourth goal flew in and Anfield rejoiced once again, Mauricio Pochettino stood on the touchline with his arms folded and turned to the Manchester United bench with an air of resignation.

Sources indicate that what can he do to improve this shambles of a team? What could anyone do? United could change their head coach every game, but without the tools to do the job, the result will be largely the same.

According to recent reports, chief executive Omar Berrada mentioned in an interview during the week that United have improved since the summer, but who is he trying to kid? They are in the relegation zone on merit, and it will need all of Pochettino's coaching powers to get them out of it.

He emerged from the tunnel shortly before 4.30pm here dressed smartly in blue, and after greeting Andoni Iraola and his staff, spent a few moments gathering his thoughts while You'll Never Walk Alone echoed around Anfield.

Sources indicate that the game plan was in tatters inside 13 minutes, though, as he watched United go two goals and one man down. There was much finger wagging from Pochettino when Leny Yoro was somewhat harshly sent off, but the decision was never going to be overturned and nor should it be used to mask another United debacle.

As the enormity of the task he has taken on dawned upon him in the second half, the Liverpool fans taunted: 'Poch is the wheel.'.

Mauricio Pochettino's first game as Man United head coach ended in a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.

The manner of the display was a microcosm of why United are mired in the relegation zone.

Pochettino made two changes to the line-up from Michael Carrick's last game in charge against Aston Villa, and the biggest of them backfired spectacularly.

Giving Matthijs de Ligt his Premier League start for more than a year against Liverpool at Anfield felt like a gamble as he replaced Harry Maguire in central defence.

'When I saw Matthijs de Ligt's name on the team-sheet I was absolutely stunned,' admitted former United defender Gary Neville on Sky Sports, citing De Ligt's performance on his only start since last November in the Champions League defeat by Como in October.

However, the Dutchman was at fault for misreading the situation that led to Yoro being sent off in the eighth minute for the foul on Alexander Isak that saw Dominik Szoboszlai fire Liverpool ahead from a free-kick, and was the nearest United defender to Florian Wirtz when he hooked in the second shortly afterwards.

De Ligt got away with falling flat on his face and allowing Isak a free run on goal just after the hour mark, but couldn't stop Bradley Barcola's cross going through his legs when Rio Ngumoha scored the third shortly afterwards.

The nightmare was complete when his ill-judged pass to Joshua Zirkzee let in Liverpool for Victor Munoz to make it 4-0.

Pochettino's other change was to leave out Amad Diallo - who has claimed a couple of memorable goals against Liverpool but hasn't scored for United in nearly a year - and play Patrick Dorgu on the left.

Dorgu returned from injury to head a dramatic late equaliser in Carrick's final game in charge, but he was deemed to be unfit for duty by Denmark who sent him home during the international break.

He started on the left side of attack but switched to left-back when Yoro was sent off and Pochettino reshuffled what is statistically the worst defence in Europe as he tried to avoid a bloodbath.

Matthijs de Ligt (right) endured a nightmare game at centre-back as United were thumped.

Pochettino's response to a horror start was to send on Maguire for Bryan Mbeumo, his best attacker, to provide extra protection for De Ligt.

Having started the game in United's familiar 4-2-3-1 formation, he switched to 5-3-1. Moving to a back-five when your team only has 10 men felt like damage limitation.

It needed some excellent saves from Senne Lammens - not to mention a crucial block by Maguire to send Isak's effort over the bar before half-time - to spare United from an embarrassing defeat on a par with the seven and five goal humiliations at the hands of Liverpool in recent years.

Even so, after seeing his team record a pitiful xG of 0.14 in a first half that saw United have one shot on target and four touches in the Liverpool box, he knew they had to pose more of an attacking threat if only to relieve the pressure on their defence.

Zirkzee replaced the anonymous Matheus Cunha at half-time in the hope that he could hold the ball up better, but the xG rose only marginally to 0.63 by the end compared to Liverpool's 4.38.

Pochettino sent on Mason Mount and Noussair Mazraoui for Youri Tielemans and Dorgu in the 65th minute, and they had only been on the pitch for a matter of seconds when Ngumoha got Liverpool's third.

Senne Lammens produced multiple save to prevent the scoreline from further embarrasment.

There are so many problems piled up for Pochettino, it will be difficult to know where to start when he returns to his desk at Carrington on Monday ahead of this week's Champions League tie against Sporting Lisbon in Portugal.

This is a team chronically short of form and confidence that has forgotten how to win. There are only so many changes he can make with the squad available until the January transfer window, so the Argentine is stuck with what he's got until then.

But United have simply got to stop giving up early goals. It was a problem that plagued Carrick against Atletico Madrid, Como, Roma and Villa, and any hope that Pochettino could stop the rot disappeared inside eight minutes here.

Yoro's red card was also United's fourth in the last eight games (and his second), which is another bad habit they will have to kick if Pochettino is going to turn this season from hell around.

Cristian Chivu alla vigilia ha suonato la carica: "È l’occasione di dimostrarsi ambiziosi".   • Maximilian Beier secured Borussia Dortmund a valuable point against unbeaten Arsenal in Tuesday night’s UEFA Champions League clash in London.
  • Sources indicate that the Bundesliga leaders had to withstand early pressure, but Viktor Gyökeres left Gregor Kobel with no chance with a superb strike after ten minutes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Maximilian Beier secured Borussia Dortmund a valuable point against unbeaten Arsenal in Tuesday night’s UEFA Champions League clash in London.

Sources indicate that the Bundesliga leaders had to withstand early pressure, but Viktor Gyökeres left Gregor Kobel with no chance with a superb strike after ten minutes. The Swede gathered the ball just outside the Dortmund penalty area, before striking it over Kobel and into the top corner. Dortmund’s custodian and Daniel Svensson then thwarted chances as the onslaught continued. “We had an extremely weak first 15 minutes, where we were very hesitant,” Nico Schlotterbeck told Amazon Prime.

Dortmund continuously looked to exploit Arsenal’s high defensive line, but it was the Gunners who had the next golden opportunity through Declan Rice, only to be thwarted by the excellent Schlotterbeck who executed a timely block on the Englishman, who was through on goal.

According to recent reports, arsenal took a slender 1-0 lead into the break, but Dortmund equalised ten minutes after the restart. Joane Gadou won the ball back in his own half before going on a superb run into the attacking third, before playing in Beier who cut back onto his left foot and slotted the ball under Kepa, who was deputising for the injured David Raya.

Recent findings suggest that that goal clearly gave Dortmund confidence, as Jobe Bellingham saw his strike ruled out for offside after following up Julian Ryerson’s parried effort. Bellingham and Beier’s departure, though, seemed to take the sting out of Dortmund’s game, as Arsenal were on top in the final 20 minutes.

First, Gyökeres missed a sitter in the 76th minute after placing his free header wide of Kobel’s post, before a goalmouth scramble ensued four minutes later. Rice then hit the post just two minutes later, but Dortmund withstood the storm to secure a share of the spoils on a bitterly cold night.

Borussia Dortmund: Kobel (7) – Gadou (7) , Anton (6), Schlotterbeck (7) – Ryerson (5), Veerman (6), Nmecha (6), Svensson (4), Bellingham (6), Beier (7) – Silva (4).

Others: Guirassy (5), Karetsas (4), Sabitzer (5), Mane (-).

GGFN | Daniel Pinder – reporting from the Emirates Stadium.

  • Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

Recent findings suggest that rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc.

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

The supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

Carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

Bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe.

It was a lovely finish after good work by the largely anonymous Matheus Cunha, and when Bentancur was sent off five minutes later after butting Luke Shaw, it should have been the cue to see out the game. To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

It has been revealed that equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

Carlos Baleba coming on around the hour mark and making a difference on his debut will at least offer Carrick some grounds for encouragement. The £65m midfield signing from Brighton offers some energy and urgency and looks a more natural bedfellow for Kobbie Mainoo than Youri Tielemans, who was woeful against Spurs and should have come off earlier.

Recent findings suggest that in truth, Tielemans was not alone. Throughout the team there was a disconnect and unease and Carrick admitted it became contagious.

In a recent development, “We just couldn’t find a way to get ourselves into the game, whether that was with the ball or without the ball,” the United manager said. “We were a little bit slow with the decision-making, didn’t quite see the passing areas, the space. You don’t want it to happen, but sometimes it can and it probably spread through the team a little bit too much.”.

It does not help that Bruno Fernandes is being hampered by an injury he has been carrying for weeks or that Carrick has no natural centre-forward to call upon with Benjamin Sesko again sidelined by the recurrence of a worrying shin problem. Amad Diallo did return here after a lengthy lay-off of his own, but did not look match fit.

In defence, Lisandro Martínez did enough to put off Dominic Solanke, who fired over from Sávio’s cross in the second half, but this was otherwise another poor showing from the Argentine centre-back, one of several positions where United need upgrades.

United needed shaking badly, but when Carrick turned to his bench he called upon Joshua Zirkzee, a fitful forward the club wanted to sell this summer, and right-back Diogo Dalot in addition to Baleba.

Sources indicate that marcus Rashford cannot have been fit given he was only introduced in the 95th minute and perhaps the same was true of the unused Mason Mount. As for £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, this was another league game when the Brazilian midfielder did not get a look in.

United fans had taunted Spurs when a goal and a man up. “You’re going down with the City,” they crowed, a nod to the possibility of City being expelled or relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching more than 100 financial rules.

Recent findings suggest that united fans had also revived their Stretford End “ticker” after reaching the conclusion that none of City’s titles under Abu Dhabi ownership had been won fairly so, in their eyes, it is now 50 years since their rivals last won anything legitimately. City, of course, continue to maintain their innocence and have lodged an appeal.

But United fans were unable to crow for too long once Solanke levelled.

In a recent development, spurs are level in stoppage-time! 😳 https://t.co/NoivNchgWw.

In a recent development, it had been similar early in the game when the home fans had trained their sights on City. “You cheating b--------, you know what you are”, they sang lustily.

But as the match wore on, those chants began to quieten as the crowd, taking their lead from the team, fell decidedly flat.

Carrick is going to have to find a spark from somewhere and promptly.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Carrick said: “It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time.

In a recent development, “But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position - we should see it through. We have to manage those situations. That’s two late goals which have hurt us, and things look very different. That’s the reality.”.

When asked about the boos at half-time and full-time, he replied: “It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”.

We have to react in all ways we can. It is a bad way, it is not the right way. I kiss Bentancur in the dressing room. Football is character.

In a recent development, “We win the game if we play as a team. We didn’t win this game playing as a team. Every game like today, we will win many games.”.

When asked about Solanke, he replied: “He is a good player for Tottenham. There for not too many strikers better than Solanke. Jobe Bellingham thought he had scored Borussia Dortmund’s go-ahead goal after Maximilian Beier had leveled proceedings against Arsenal, but the Englishman was marginally offside after following up Julian Ryerson’s parried effort as Die Schwarzgelben secured a valuable point against last season’s finalists.

It has been revealed that speaking in the mixed zone, attended by Get German Football News, Bellingham reflected on the deserved point against unbeaten Arsenal. “The team is quite proud,” he explained. “To take a point in the end is probably fair, and it feels good.

Sources indicate that “We were in a difficult place and still managed to get a positive result. The performance improved as the game went on. We didn’t have a great start, and they were fully committed from the beginning. Just as expected, Arsenal are a top team.”.

After a difficult first season in Dortmund, Bellingham is starting to find his feet. The Englishman has started BVB’s last six games across all competitions, and is establishing himself alongside Felix Nmecha and Joey Veerman, which, in turn, saw him nominated for England’s senior squad for the first time over the November international break.

Against Arsenal, Bellingham covered a lot of ground and recorded three defensive actions. The 21-year-old also looked to progress the ball, playing eight passes into the final third, and four line-break passes.

GGFN | Daniel Pinder – reporting from the Emirates Stadium.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

RB Leipzig climbed into the UEFA Champions League play-off spots with a 3-1 win over French outfit Lens, thanks largely to a superb performance from the in-form Antonio Nusa, who was twice on target as the Bundesliga outfit dominated.

On paper, the hosts had what can only be described as a huge chance to get their hands on a massive three points, facing a team that took the heaviest of beatings when the league phase was last in action – having shipped nine against Como, and they didn’t waste the opportunity.

Leipzig boss Martín Demichelis made three changes from the win over Union Berlin at the weekend, bringing in Maxime Esteve for Castello Lukeba at the back, Rocco Reitz for Ezechiel Banzuzi in midfield and Tidiam Gomis for Romulo up top.

Recent findings suggest that beginning the game on the front foot, Leipzig immediately pushed the French visitors deep into their own half. Antonio Nusa jinked his way into a couple of early shooting positions, before misfiring, but it didn’t take long for the first goal to arrive. After five minutes, Tidiam Gomis earned a free kick on the very edge of the Lens area. David Raum did the rest, scoring with the help of a hefty deflection.

It has been revealed that just a few minutes later, the lively Nusa latched on to a loose defensive pass, before slotting home coolly, making it 2-0 before the ten-minute mark. Abdallah Sima then got free in the Leipzig box, but couldn’t get his shot off, instead losing his footing and delivering a disappointing end to one of Lens’ only promising first-half moves.

For most of the first half, it was the home team in charge, pushing forward at every opportunity, with the visitors mustering little, both in terms of defensive nous and offensive punch.

Leipzig very nearly made it three after the restart, Brajan Gruda coming close, only to be denied by Robin Risser.

The visitors then upped their efforts, forging a number of early second-half attacks through Florian Thauvin, who failed to accurately deliver several corners, before shooting from just outside the box, only to see his effort blocked by a defender.

It wasn’t long, though, until the Lens pressure paid off, with Matthieu Udol pulling back on 58 minutes. The French midfielder latched onto a loose ball inside the box and rifled home. Four minutes later and Sima thought that he’d levelled things, only for the offside flag to cut short the celebrations of the Senegalese forward.

The Lens players were clearly galvanised by Udol’s goal, which was followed by more visiting pressure, and as the influential Thauvin started to see more and more of the ball, an equaliser seemed nowhere near as unlikely as it did earlier in the contest.

As the game entered the final 15 minutes, the hosts wrestled back some control, alleviating the pressure by retaining possession, before launching a couple of late counter attacks, one of which very nearly restored the two-goal lead, with substitute Christopher Nkunku being denied by the leaping Robin Risser.

Risser’s late efforts ended up being for nothing when Antonio Nusa sealed the three points in stoppage time, tapping home from an Nkunku pull back, capping off what was a Man of the Match performance, pushing Leipzig into the play-off places.

RB Leipzig: Vandevoordt (6) – Raum (7), Esteve (6), Orban (6), Baku (6) – El Aynaoui (6), Reitz (7) – Nusa (9), Baumgartner (7), Gruda (7) – Gomis (7).

Others: Romulo (6), Banzuzi (6), Nkunku (7), Seiwald (6), Maksimovic (-).

Lens: Risser (6) – Todibo (5), Baidoo (5), Ganiou (5) – Udol (7), Haidara (5), Titraoui (6), Abdulhamid (5) – Thauvin (7), Sotoca (5) – Sima (5).

Others: Kadile (5), Mesloub (5), Skoras (5), Bulatovic (-).

The Norwegian forward is in red-hot form right now, and that shone through the moment the game kicked off. His pace and direct approach caused countless problems for the Lens defence, who failed to handle a player, who can just as easily beat a man on the outside and cross or cut in and shoot.

Nusa’s second required little effort, but demonstrated that he has the off-ball movement to score poacher-type goals.

Fabrizio Romano ha ulteriormente approfondito una situazione di mercato seguita dall'Inter. Il giornalista esperto di calciomercato ha approfondito lo scenario relativo a Varela, attaccante del Monza che piace all'Inter ma non solo. A Scommesse.io Romano ha ricordato: "Il calciomercato di gennaio è sempre più vicino e c’è già chi si muove, non solo ai piani più alti della classifica. C’è chi lotta per non retrocedere, un mercato di idee che spesso va anticipato pur lasciando spazio alle occasioni last minute di una finestra veloce come quella invernale. In prima fila c’è il futuro di un uomo solo al comando: Gustavo Varela è la stella più inaspettata di questo inizio di stagione in Serie A, una perla scovata dal Monza per poco più di 2 milioni di euro e oggi nella lista dei top club dopo i suoi gol no-stop in questi primi tre mesi di stagione. Ma riveliamo prima un dettaglio: il Benfica non avrà alcuna clausola di riacquisto, non può riportare indietro Varela in forma automatica. Il club portoghese ha una clausola per l’incasso del 20% sulla futura plusvalenza in caso di cessione, e una clausola di matching rights, ovvero può pareggiare le offerte di altri club. Ma l’ultima parola spetterà comunque al giocatore: il Benfica non ha un potere ‘totale’ sull’operazione".

"Per questo si sono messi in fila già molti club, soprattutto in Italia: l’Inter è andata quattro volte a seguire Varela dal vivo col direttore Dario Baccin, ma non ha ancora affondato il colpo perché in attacco si ritiene coperta e competitiva, più un’idea per l’estate a meno che non si decida di cambiare strategia", ha aggiunto Romano sulle intenzioni dei nerazzurri. "Il Napoli ha già incontrato i suoi agenti, i rapporti sono eccellenti col direttore Manna dopo le operazioni Rafa Marin e Alisson Santos con la stessa agenzia. La Juve si è informata sul prezzo: il Monza per una cifra intorno ai 30/35 milioni di euro può davvero vendere Varela già a gennaio, attenzione perché il prezzo è fissato e i club stranieri iniziano a fiutare l'idea e scrutare i progressi di Gustavo, non possiamo escludere blitz e colpi di scena. Dovesse arrivare la cessione, si tratterebbe di una grave perdita che potrebbe intaccare le quote salvezza del Monza", ha concluso il giornalista.

Borussia Dortmund captain Nico Schlotterbeck made a superb block to deny Declan Rice from doubling Arsenal’s tally shortly after Viktor Gyökeres fired the hosts into a ten-minute lead.

Although going behind early, it could have been far worse for Dortmund, who managed to whether the storm. “We had an extremely weak first 15 minutes, in which we were very hesitant and were lucky not to concede a second goal,” Schlotterbeck told Amazon Prime at the final whistle. “We were very sluggish and couldn’t get out of our own half at all.”.

Dortmund did, though, respond just ten minutes into the second half when Maximilian Beier coolly slotted the ball under Kepa, to level the tie and secure his side a share of the spoils. “In the second half, the lads did really well,” added Schlotterbeck. “We broke them down with intensity. We went man-to-man throughout the second half and won our duels.

It has been revealed that “In the last 15 minutes, Arsenal applied a bit more pressure but the lads really fought for this point. As captain, I’m very satisfied.”.

Borussia Dortmund’s 1-1 draw leaves Schlotterbeck and Co. on ten points from a possible 15 with three wins, one draw and one defeat.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shortly before Maximilian Beier’s equaliser in Borussia Dortmund’s 1-1 draw against Arsenal in the UEFA Champions League on Tuesday night, the Bundesliga leaders believe they should have been awarded a penalty when Viktor Gyökeres handled the ball with an outstretched arm in the area.

Referee Maurizio Mariani, however, waved play on and his decision wasn’t overruled by the VAR.

It has been revealed that “I can’t explain it anymore,” said Niko Kovač. “I don’t know what constitutes as handball and what doesn’t.” BVB captain Nico Schlotterbeck also weighed in on the decision, adding: “I have a feeling we should have had a handball penalty following a corner.”.

Patrick Ittrich, who refereed in the Bundesliga between 2016 and 2026, also believes Dortmund should have been awarded a penalty. “For me, it was a clear penalty,” he told Prime Video.

Industry observers note that “I think the only argument is that one could think the player slightly pulled his arm back, but he only pulled it back when the ball was already on his hand. He actually wanted to head it, realised: ‘I can’t reach it,’ and then raised his elbow and clearly played the ball with his hand.”.

Recent findings suggest that “That’s an extended body surface, there’s a hint of intent involved. For me that’s a clear penalty.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that just when the Premier League and the world outside of east Manchester and Abu Dhabi needed Liverpool to step up, to strike back, to make a point, they faltered. Maybe it was unfair to expect them to do so, given the circumstances. But unfairness, lack of clarity and uncertainty are all prevailing moods in English football at present.

How we had rubbed our hands in anticipation of Manchester City having to play their first league fixture here at Anfield after being found guilty of industrial-scale fraud with 114 of the 115 financial charges being proven against them.

Industry observers note that it felt apt that it was at the home of Liverpool, who, along with Arsenal, possess the strongest sense of grievance at having been denied trophies and glory by City’s cheating. As expected, there were banners everywhere at Anfield. “A generation of supporters cheated,” one read and it summed up the depth of the anger.

Recent findings suggest that their fans would surely create the kind of bear-pit atmosphere that would leave City in no doubt at the vitriol that will rain down on them from now on. At every away ground. Liverpool could set the tone. The defiance.

It later amends the statement to “wherever wrongdoing is established”.

The UAE then warns Andy Burnham that it will pull billions of pounds of investment out of the UK in retaliation for the guilty verdict against City.

City argue that their sponsorship deals were part-funded by the Abu Dhabi government, rather than the club’s owners, in their appeal, which claims bank statements and witness accounts provide “irrefutable evidence” to support their case.

Bayern Munich will be without Harry Kane for the next three months after England’s leading goalscorer underwent successful surgery on a torn syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle, sustained during their Bundesliga draw against Cologne on 20 October. And with Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry and Michael Olise all sidelined, options in attack remain short for Vincent Kompany.

Olise also sustained an injury during their 1-1 draw against Cologne, but the Frenchman only suffered bruising and should return for their Bundesliga game against Hamburg on Saturday. However, Bayern must first navigate a difficult Champions League tie against French outfit Lille on Wednesday night.

In a recent development, kicker suggest that Lennart Karl will lead the attack, supported by Konrad Laimer, Tom Bischof and Nathaniel Brown. Luis Diaz is expected to return after an injury lay-off, but only to the bench, while Jamal Musiala is also expected to feature on the bench.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bayern Munich have announced that constructive talks have been held with Jamal Musiala’s management following the player’s health condition, which has been a hot topic of late.

As widely reported, Musiala has symptoms resembling absence seizures linked to a neurological disorder, with Bayern further adding that the player’s health is the top priority for both parties and that Musiala will receive full support throughout his recovery.

The statement further clarified that Musiala was first examined for symptoms on 22 April 2025, which took place in consultation with Bayern and its medical department, immediately after the neurological symptoms first appeared.

Germany’s record champions were heavily criticized for how they handled the situation following statements from Uli Hoeneß and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge.

According to recent reports, hoeneß stated: “We’re in a dilemma with him. He has an illness that cannot simply be cured, but can be managed to some extent with medication. However, whether he will ever regain the level of performance he once had remains uncertain. He is still receiving his salary, of course. But just imagine if Bayern were now to question his contract and say: ‘What he is capable of delivering now is no longer what was stipulated in the contract.'”.

Rummenigge echoed this statement, commenting about a potential pay cut for Musiala. “We would have to speak with his family, the player himself and his agency. Because, in that situation, those figures would simply no longer be financially justifiable, with all due respect,” he added.

In response to this, FIFPRO strongly condemned Bayern Munich’s leadership, accusing the club of a “coordinated strategy” to publicly pressure Musiala into renegotiating his contract.

Now Bayern have said that the club and Musiala’s management have agreed to continue their discussions “in a spirit of partnership and confidentiality.”.

We weren’t as good in the second half as we had been in the first,” he stated, further adding that the team lacked confidence on the ball and made a lot of mistakes: “Lens changed their approach and were the better side. There are things we need to address.”.

Demichelis also discussed the importance of enjoying the win: “We need to learn to enjoy moments like these. I congratulated the boys and told them that tonight wasn’t the time to be disappointed or have doubts. We can enjoy this win tonight,” he added.

Sources indicate that regarding possible fatigue, he said they will try to utilize rotation going forward, even though that is not the problem at the moment: “That wasn’t our problem today, but fatigue will start to become a factor over the next few games. We’ll try to manage that by rotating the squad and sharing out the playing time. We need everyone in the squad.”.

Leipzig will travel to Old Trafford to face Manchester United in their next Champions League game but before that, they have important Bundesliga games against Freiburg and Mainz, while they will face Bayer Leverkusen in the DFB Pokal.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

Published: 08:08 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 18:17 EST, 24 November 2026.

Having summoned Luca Williams-Barnett to his office to let the teenager know he would be making his first Premier League start, Roberto De Zerbi could not resist a little bit of fun.

De Zerbi cast a serious demeanour and told him he had weighed the options and figured the best course of action would be 60 minutes with the Under-21s.

According to recent reports, williams-Barnett did not hide his disappointment. 'Why, do you think you are ready to start for the first team?' asked the Spurs boss. The 18-year-old said he thought so.

De Zerbi cracked a smile and told him he was in the team against Ipswich but demanded two things in return.

First, that his young star would play with freedom as though 'in the park with friends' and second that he would work without the ball in the manner of the world's best players in his position, such as Lamine Yamal.

This is where the comparisons to Yamal emerged soon after Williams-Barnett lit up the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. On Tuesday, he was rewarded for his progress with a upcoming contract at the club.

Industry observers note that he said: 'This is a special moment for me and my family, and one I have worked really hard to reach. But this is only the start.

Luca Williams-Barnett scored his first Premier League goal for Tottenham on his first start in the top flight.

The talented academy youngster may not be lightning fast but he has pace and creates goals.

Sources indicate that 'Spurs is a family to me. I've been here for so long – it's a second home, where I trust the people and coaches who have pushed me to become the player I am today.

'The club has trusted and believed in me, now I'm ready to repay that.'.

Hopes are indeed high. Similarities with Yamal are evident in physique, his fluency of movement on the ball and the bursts of pace, the way they look to play. Even the hairstyle.

Just as Yamal, a left footer, likes to operate wide on the right for Barcelona and Spain, De Zerbi deployed Williams-Barnett as a right footer on the left, although most of his youth career has been spent centrally in the No 10 position.

He does not possess what you would consider in modern football to be exceptional pace, but he is quick, and his strengths are on the ball. He likes the ball. He creates. And he scores goals.

From wide on the left against Ipswich, he scored within 15 minutes, darting in at the back post to finish, and created the second for Dominic Solanke, with a 60-yard run from inside his own half and cross with his left foot.

According to recent reports, his brilliance lit up the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, where there has not been a lot to celebrate in the last 18 months. Terrible home form was the crux of last season's relegation fears.

Here, they rose to salute a fresh talent, one of their own. One De Zerbi believes has the attitude to match his outrageous talent. Confident, certainly. Aware of his natural gifts and his technical skills. Perhaps bordering on arrogance when on the pitch.

De Zerbi was pleased to see Williams-Barnett, in a seat nearby on the team bus from the training ground to the stadium, watching YouTube clips of Ronaldinho, Eden Hazard and Neymar.

The Spurs boss, who has faith in the power of inspirational video footage, took this as a positive sign. The youngster was relaxed but more than this he had a passion for football and always looking to learn.

'I'm positive about his character and behaviour because I've been working with him for three or four months and I know him enough,' said De Zerbi, whose tactical instructions involved James Maddison operating closely to Williams-Barnett, a kindred spirit in a footballing sense able to talk him through the game.

When the teenager set off on the swaggering run for Solanke's goal, Maddison could be seen nearby urging him forward into the ocean of space left open by Ipswich.

The 18-year-old had rival clubs circling but Spurs have now tied him down.

Born and raised in Luton, Williams-Barnett comes from a strong, grounded family - which will only help as he looks to assimilate into the senior side.

It has been revealed that spurs have prioritised Premier League experience in the transfer market under De Zerbi to create a more mature dressing room environment. Signings such as Andy Robertson have been key to this.

The policy is not purely for the benefit of academy graduates stepping into the first-team environment, but it does help when it comes to setting the standards required in elite sport.

Anyone gifted enough to break into the Spurs squad will have been feted as a star through the youth development phase and well rewarded to resist others trying to lure them away.

Williams-Barnett was under contract until 2028 but his fresh deal means clubs circling must now look elsewhere.

It is easy for impressionable teens to become conceited in this situation. Williams-Barnett has had discipline and time-keeping issues but most at Spurs speak of a young man devoted to his football from a strong, loving family who are sure to keep him grounded.

He was born and raised in Luton, starting out in Luton Town's pre-academy to Under 10s, before Spurs paid a small fee for him.

His father Jonathan Barnett was a central midfielder in Step Three of non-league football, known as 'Jono' and playing for various clubs in the region including Dunstable Town and Arlesey Town and renowned for his passing, set pieces and with an eye for goal.

According to recent reports, although more of a dribbler, Luca grew up with football in the family, polishing his technical skills with his dad in the back garden. 'He is from a very good family and it's crucial for this type of players,' mentioned De Zerbi.

Spurs have been here before, of course, with talented teens breaking through with N17 at their feet.

There was Mikey Moore's wonderful cameo against AZ Alkmaar after which Ange Postecoglou called for patience and commonsense, and Maddison went on TV and said it was 'like having Neymar on the left wing'.

There was Jose Mourinho taking the match ball from Son Heung-min, who had just scored the most incredible solo goal against Burnley, and handing it to Troy Parrott on his Premier League debut.

Recent findings suggest that there was Mauricio Pochettino dubbing Marcus Edwards his 'mini Messi'. Pochettino soon came to wish he had not burdened Edwards with such lavish praise.

In a recent development, the pitfalls are well known and progress is rarely a smooth upward trajectory. It is a balancing act between maximising potential and getting carried away.

De Zerbi is quietly confident Williams-Barnett has what it takes to handle the hype.

On the fresh deal, thought to be for five years, the manager mentioned: 'Luca is a player I think the world of, and I'm so happy that he has signed a new contract.

'He has benefitted from being around the first team every day, growing in stature and consistency, and has deserved his place in the matchday squad over recent weeks.

'Everyone can see how technically gifted Luca is on the pitch but I also love his calmness and decision-making under pressure.

In a recent development, 'The best players have confidence on the pitch and humility off it. There is still plenty of room for Luca to improve, and I know he will continue to work hard every day to be the best version of himself.'.

In a recent development, L'Inter segue con grandissima attenzione l'attaccante del Monza Gustavo Varela. Sulle tracce del portoghese ci sono anche altre big, il Monza fiuta l'affare. Repubblica racconta come il club brianzolo ha scovato il giocatore:.

"Il Monza lo ha preso dal Benfica per appena 2 milioni più 1,5 di bonus e il 20% della futura rivendita. Il club di Lisbona si è riservato il diritto di pareggiare eventuali offerte. Difficilmente, però, Gustavo farà marcia indietro. Tutti lo vogliono. Lunedì contro la Fiorentina in tribuna al Brianteo c'erano gli osservatori dell'Inter. In coda a sgomitare anche Napoli (che ha già parlato con il suo agente, Hector Paris), Juventus, Barcellona, Liverpool e Arsenal", sottolinea Repubblica.

Recent findings suggest that "Potevano pensarci prima, certo. Però Varela non è stato un colpo di fortuna per il Monza, che usa un sistema codificato per scovare talenti da valorizzare. Alla base c'è un software, sviluppato dall'ad Baldissoni e dal suo gruppo di lavoro – di cui faceva parte Francesco Vallone, oggi coordinatore dell'area tecnica in Brianza – ai tempi della Roma. Hanno iniziato a metterlo a punto nel 2011, poi lo hanno affinato e migliorato. Oggi la piattaforma monitora in tempo reale oltre 60mila calciatori di tutto il mondo, guardando sia alle serie principali sia a quelle minori. Non mette insieme solo statistiche: valuta e combina i dati atletici dei giocatori e le loro qualità. Un esempio: evidenzia il tipo di giocata che viene fatta in un determinato contesto e zona di campo, la capacità di incidere nei momenti delicati della partita (ha un peso diverso segnare l'1-0 o il 4-0). Somma una serie di dati e permette pure la comparazione con altri profili: ho bisogno di un terzino, ne trovo uno che mi piace, lo posso confrontare con elementi simili. Insomma, un metodo scientifico applicato al calcio".

"La piattaforma aiuta ad analizzare e fare una scrematura, poi c'è l'occhio umano. I giocatori trovati con il software vengono visionati sul campo dagli scout. Il club brianzolo ne ha oltre 10, assegnati in diverse aree, che completano l'opera. È andata così con Varela, segnalato e seguito da più osservatori nel periodo in cui era in prestito al Gil Vicente. Lo sono andati a vedere pure alcuni dirigenti, come Vallone e l'ex ds Burdisso. È successa la stessa cosa con Foe Ondoa (20 anni), preso dall'Estoril Praia per 1,5 milioni, e con Jay Robinson (19 anni), prelevato dal Southampton in prestito solo perché gli inglesi non hanno voluto concedere opzioni di acquisto. Anche in questi casi, la sensazione è che il Monza – la squadra con l'età media più bassa della A – ci abbia visto lungo".

"Non è finita qui. Dopo la piattaforma e gli scout, per chi arriva viene preparato un programma di lavoro individuale, volto a migliorare determinate caratteristiche. Un percorso costruito a tavolino, che mira a migliorare i punti deboli con allenamenti specifici. Per Varela, era stata individuata come carenza la capacità di calciare con il piede debole, il sinistro. Su quello Gustavo ha lavorato, accanto alle sedute con i compagni. Il risultato di questo percorso, con lui, è stato incredibile. Per prenderlo ora servono non meno di 40 milioni: dovesse arrivare un'offerta del genere già a gennaio, difficilmente il Monza potrebbe opporre resistenza. Ma, intanto, sta già cercando la prossima gemma", chiude Repubblica.

Dopo l’esperienza nella FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival, andata in scena dal 24 al 30 ottobre in Azerbaigian e conclusa al dodicesimo posto, la Nazionale Under 15 tornerà in campo dal 27 al 29 novembre a Novarello per il consueto appuntamento annuale con il Torneo di Natale.

It has been revealed that il tecnico Enrico Battisti ha convocato per l’occasione 66 calciatori, tutti nati nel 2012, con l’unica eccezione dell’attaccante classe 2013 del Genoa, Alessandro Criscito, figlio d’arte di Domenico – 26 presenze e un gol con la Nazionale A – e fratello di Alfredo, anch’egli in forza ai liguri, che compare nell’elenco dei difensori. I convocati saranno suddivisi in tre squadre (Selezione A, Selezione B e Selezione C), composte da 22 elementi ciascuna, che si affronteranno in un torneo triangolare all’italiana.

Portieri: Christian Basso (Torino), Leonardo Brigante (Torino), Gianluca D’Alfonso (Monza), Gian Piero Maria Galliera (Inter), Mattia Manca (Roma), Vittorio Zazzera (Como);.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newcastle United suffered a painful, chastening defeat, comprehensively beaten by Coventry City in a performance that should send a shudder of fear through Tyneside.

Sources indicate that it was a dreadful night for the visitors, who conceded four goals for the second successive away game. The manner in which they fell apart was damning. Whatever the supposed style of play, it is not good to watch: long balls are pumped forward for short strikers to chase or compete for in the air against far taller centre-backs. Away from home, it is becoming ineffective.

Newcastle are too easy to create chances against and there is not much that gets you excited when they attack.

Matthias Jaissle’s side did create chances against Coventry, but are not clinical and do not inspire confidence they can be with the players they have. Defensively, they escaped earlier in the season, but are now being exposed and punished. “Not good enough in both boxes,” was Jaissle’s blunt verdict. “To concede eight goals in two away games is not good enough.”.

Matthias Jaissle on this evening's defeat at the Coventry Building Society Arena. https://t.co/216NW6Laz8.

Newcastle’s misery was in stark contrast to the joyous celebrations from Coventry. This was a thoroughly deserved first home win of the season for Frank Lampard’s side.

According to recent reports, “It was an outstanding performance,” the manager stated. “We knew we would have to suffer at times against a team like Newcastle. But we were really good at the basics, winning the second balls, winning the duels, those moments are critical. It’s not always about pretty patterns, it’s about work ethic.”.

The win lifts Coventry level on points with Manchester United and will give them fresh confidence at this level. This could be the start of something special for them.

As for Newcastle, this raises uncomfortable questions about their summer recruitment, with so many expensive players on the bench or playing badly. A win for Newcastle United this evening will take Matthias Jaissle’s side up to fourth in the Premier League and vindicate the members of the club’s hierarchy who insisted they had appointed an elite manager to replace Eddie Howe.

It will also suggest they got their summer rebuild right and everything will point to an exciting future for a newly introduced look team.

Yet, should Newcastle lose against a Coventry City side – newly promoted to the top flight and yet to win at home this season – ripples of discontent will spread through the fanbase and everything about the summer, from managerial appointment to player recruitment will be called into question.

Recent findings suggest that that may seem like an odd thing to write given how wildly different those reactions are but that is where Newcastle find themselves at the moment. We do not actually know if they are any good or what the expectations should be for a young team with a rookie Premier League head coach.

There remains an undercurrent of anxiety among supporters who have seen so many of their best players leave over the last 12 months and be replaced by young, emerging talent from across Europe.

In a recent development, the 4-1 thrashing at Leeds in their last away game was a painful reminder of the team’s vulnerability. They were bullied and outclassed.

Newcastle have not put together an impressive 90-minute performance since the opening day draw with Liverpool, yet that defeat to Leeds was also the only game they have lost. in all competitions. We will know a lot more about them after this. This is a game they are expected to win, so the ramifications of a defeat will be more severe.

When Brian Kilcline was at Notts County, the manager Jimmy Sirrel became a little perturbed by the nickname his young centre-back had carried since his school days. It might have been nice alliteration, but “Killer Kilcline” was not exactly the image he wanted his team to portray.

“Also the lads shouting, ‘get him Killer’ tended to alert referees,” Kilcline recalls.

According to recent reports, so Sirrel decided he would put it to the County fans. He organised a competition to establish a better moniker for his foursquare defender.

Recent findings suggest that “You know what they came up with?” Kilcline indicates. “Curly Wurly. Like the chocolate bar. It was to do with my hair, which was naturally curled. By the way, it was never a perm. But I mean, come on. I can’t imagine Curly Wurly would have intimidated anyone.”.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Coventry City and Newcastle United from the Ricoh Arena. Newcastle have played only once there in the league – a 4-1 victory in the Championship back in 2010 when Chris Hughton’s side stormed the league. Their last top-flight visit to the city was way back in 2000, the year Cov’s 34-season spell in the top division ended. Alan Shearer Kevin Gallacher scored at Highfield Road on that occasion, a year after they were sent packing 4-1 by Gordon Strachan’s side by virtue of goals from Carlton Palmer, Paul Williams, Robbie Keane and Mustapha Hadji.

Today’s visit begins with Newcastle in 11th, having bounced back from their Monday night mauling at Elland Road to beat Hull 23 days ago. So bunched is the table, though, that victory tonight would propel them up to fourth. Coventry, by contrast, are 19th after one win and four defeats from their opening five games. If they win they would join Manchester United on six points and leap to 14th, one place ahead of Nottingham Forest, the team they beat last time out before the international break.

Frank Lampard’s side responded superbly after being hammered 5-0 by Brighton in their last home game, tightening up in midfield and defence and finding precisely Forest’s weak spots that Oliver Glasner has been unable so far to armour-plate. Taiwo Awoniyi, who was sent off during that defeat by Brighton, is absent serving the second leg of his three-match suspension and Hajii Wright and Aurele Amenda are still some way off returning. Tino Livramento pulled out of the England camp with injury and is likely to be sidelined for a while longer but Matthias Jaissle was more optimistic about his raft of other doubts: William Osula, Lewis Miley, Amar Dedic, club captain Dan Burn, Anthony Elanga and Jacob Ramsey.

In a recent development, il futuro di Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg torna al centro delle discussioni in casa Olympique Marsiglia. Il centrocampista danese, accostato con insistenza alla Juventus e alla Fiorentina in vista del mercato di gennaio, ha parlato della propria situazione durante la conferenza stampa alla vigilia della sfida di Europa League contro il Levski Sofia. Parole che raccontano il desiderio di continuare la sua esperienza in Francia, ma anche qualche retroscena sulle indiscrezioni che lo hanno accompagnato negli ultimi mesi. "Quest'anno ho avuto la sensazione che qualcuno volesse che me ne andassi", ha ammesso il numero 23 dell'OM.

Il danese ha innanzitutto voluto chiarire il proprio rapporto con il club e con i suoi sostenitori, sottolineando come non tutte le notizie circolate sul suo conto corrispondano alla realtà: "A volte si dicono delle cose sulla stampa e non sempre sono vere. Quest'anno ho sentito che qualcuno voleva che me ne andassi. Non posso presentarmi ogni giorno davanti alla sala stampa: tutto quello che posso fare è concentrarmi su ciò che mi chiede l'allenatore e cercare di rappresentare questa maglia nel miglior modo possibile. Amo giocare per il Marsiglia, l'ho detto anche al tecnico l'altro giorno".

Sources indicate that hojbjerg ha poi ribadito la propria volontà di proseguire l'avventura in Francia, ricordando anche la posizione assunta durante la scorsa estate: "Sentire continuamente che sto per partire è qualcosa con cui bisogna convivere, ma non tutto quello che viene detto è vero. Personalmente mi vedo al Marsiglia finché non ci sarò più. Quest'estate volevo restare e fare tutto il possibile per riuscirci. Sono davvero molto orgoglioso di giocare per l'OM, un club straordinario".

Sources indicate that un legame che il centrocampista ha spiegato anche attraverso il rapporto con la tifoseria: "Una cosa che condivido con i sostenitori è la passione. È vero che sono scandinavo, ma questa passione la sento anch'io ed è ciò che conta. Il resto non posso controllarlo. Apprezzo ogni volta che scendo in campo e darò tutto finché vestirò questa maglia".

Antonio Nocerino, allenatore del Napoli Primavera, ha parlato dopo la sconfitta contro il Manchester City per 4-1 in Youth League:.

“Siamo partiti male. Sembra che quando giochiamo queste partite si pensi di più a quello che c’è intorno, al rispetto per l’altra squadra, e non si pensi più a ciò che si deve fare in campo. Ai ragazzi per il secondo tempo ho detto di mettere ciò che avevano, di giocare, perché non avevano nulla da perdere, con coraggio e intensità. Abbiamo avuto delle opportunità, abbiamo preso una traversa, poi ci sono state delle situazioni a nostro favore che potevano essere finalizzate in maniera diversa. Mi porto a casa la reazione, l’approccio della ripresa, ovviamente sapendo anche contro chi abbiamo giocato. Va dato anche merito all’avversario, sono forti.

Sources indicate that club Brugge? Noi in tutte le partite vogliamo provare a fare risultato, anche lì, se dobbiamo chiudere, dobbiamo farlo nel migliore dei modi. Dev’esserci sempre quella speranza che non deve mai mancare. Dobbiamo giocarcela come sempre, l’obiettivo è fare bene e portare soprattutto in casa a vincere. È un sogno però ci vogliamo provare fino alla fine.

Campionato e Coppa Italia? Dobbiamo lavorare bene e recuperare le forze, oltre a mettere una mentalità un po’ diversa. Dobbiamo cercare di essere più aggressivi, vogliosi, più forti nell’uno contro uno e finalizzare un po’ di più quello che creiamo. Costruiamo tanto, arriviamo negli ultimi metri, ma abbiamo poca cattiveria nel chiudere l’azione. È una situazione secondo me individuale e mentale di ogni singolo giocatore. Noi alleniamo tanto i tiri e le situazioni di gioco, però poi c’è anche l’individualità del giocatore. Quando noi ti mettiamo in una condizione di tirare o di fare l’azione da gol, bisogna avere la cattiveria, la fame di fare gol. A noi manca un po’ questo. Finora siamo stati un po’ troppo ‘belli’, e in alcune situazioni dobbiamo essere un po’ più sporchi”.

"Fabregas è un tecnico visionario, porta qualcosa di nuovo ed efficace. Può diventare un top, in un grande club potrà davvero diventare grande". E' il pensiero di mister Moreno Longo, che ai microfoni della radio di Tuttomercatoweb.com ha detto la sua sul tecnico del Como. "Oggi è in una zona di comfort, dove si è incastrato tutto, ora dovrà confermare tutto quello di buono che si dice su di lui, in un grande club", ha aggiunto a Maracanà.

E a chi parla di presunzione da parte del tecnico spagnolo, risponde così: "Ci può stare, ma credo che rispecchi il fatto che l'allenatore debba trasferire le proprie idee. Per convincere gli altri, deve essere il primo a crederci, anche con la comunicazione. per me è persuasivo, con i giocatori che ti pesano in ogni frangente. Ogni cosa che dici deve essere poi riscontrabile in campo. E oggi lo vedi nel Como, che è una squadra completa. Fa gol e ne prende pochi, è un modo di attaccare che non ti espone a grossi rischi difensivi".

Recent findings suggest that longo che poi sul discorso Como ha chiuso dicendo: "E' stato fatto un mercato veramente fatto bene. Ci sono giocatori che non so quanti club avrebbero preso per centrare certi obiettivi importanti. Fabregas dovrà fare uno step in alto che dovrà confermare quanto di buono sta facendo oggi. Gasperini per esempio è andato a Roma, con una squadra più forte, con più qualità, è sta facendo bene comunque per esempio. I suoi principi sono validi, nel top club cambia la gestione dei campioni, che è differente".

Recent findings suggest that infine sulla lotta per salvarsi, che vede oggi diverse squadre tra cui alcuni nomi eccellenti, il mister ha detto: "Venezia, Lecce e Parma e Monza sono gli organici che hanno qualcosa in meno. Poi vediamo che ci sono altre invischiate e il problema lì è nella testa. Quando non sei abituato a stare lì e speravi in un altro campionato, pensi inconsciamente che ne esci ma poi il tempo passa e rimani lì...Sassuolo, Udinese e Fiorentina faticano a trovare continuità, poi ci sono contestazioni e fatichi ad uscirne fuori e rischi più di altre".

Bayern Munich slammed as 'despicable' and accused of 'co-ordinated' plot to undermine Jamal Musiala after club chief questioned star's contract due to his health issues - with Jude Bellingham, Michael Olise and Rio Ferdinand backing the youngster

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 10:38 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 11:29 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • Bayern Munich have come under criticism from FIFA's players' union and leading figures in the game amid accusations that the club is attempting to slash Jamal Musiala's wages following his diagnosis with a 'neurological dysfunction'.
  • The Germany international was diagnosed over the summer with absence seizures, a form of epilepsy which causes 'brief but easily treatable seizures'.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 10:38 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 11:29 EST, 23 November 2026.

Bayern Munich have come under criticism from FIFA's players' union and leading figures in the game amid accusations that the club is attempting to slash Jamal Musiala's wages following his diagnosis with a 'neurological dysfunction'.

The Germany international was diagnosed over the summer with absence seizures, a form of epilepsy which causes 'brief but easily treatable seizures'.

Musiala shocked the sporting world when he collapsed in two matches earlier this season, with Bayern manager Vincent Kompany explaining that the player had suffered from a reaction to a change in his medication.

Comments from members of Bayern's hierarchy have sparked controversy in Germany and abroad, with senior figures appearing to question the length of the player's contract – which runs until 2030 – should Musiala not recover his form.

Honorary president Uli Hoeness was the first to speak out on the potential drop-off in form Musiala might suffer with long-term absences, claiming earlier this month that he 'may never regain the performance level he once had'.

'We are facing a dilemma in this case, as he is suffering from an illness that cannot simply be cured, but it can be controlled to a certain extent with the use of medication,' Hoeness told German outlet BR24.

Fifpro and international footballers have come out in support of Musiala over concerns that Bayern Munich might reduce his salary.

Both Uli Hoeness and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge have made comments suggesting consequences should Musiala not return to his level.

Jan-Christian Dreesen also suggested that the club would need to 'assess' the situation if his performances do not return to their high heights.

Chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen then backed up Hoeness's comments and implied that Musiala's contract may need to be 'assessed'.

'We're monitoring his level of play. He'll certainly need time to improve further – like any injured player,' Dreesen noted in discussion with AZ. 'And then we need to calmly assess the situation and, if necessary, sit down with his family and management.

'Either we'll all be happy together and he'll be the same Jamal he always was – or, if he's a different Jamal along the way, we'll have to discuss it.'.

According to recent reports, 'If we're not consistently at a level that also aligns with the economic realities, then we'll have to talk to each other. Nevertheless, we have a valid contract, and that's the end of it.'.

Recent findings suggest that the 23-year-old is one of Bayern's highest-earners, having signed a deal with the club to extend his time in Bavaria in February 2025. The deal is thought to be worth £18.4million per year.

Adding fuel to the fire days later was former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, who told Sky Sports/RTL that he thought it was almost reasonable to discuss a renegotiation should Musiala not return to the level at which he once played.

'That is certainly possible and cannot be ruled out,' he said. 'Unfortunately, what we know suggests that it will be difficult to reach the level that he has so often shown here in this stadium.'.

'We need to talk to the family, the player, and above all, the agency. Because then these sums are – sorry, with all due respect – no longer feasible.

According to recent reports, 'I can't imagine Jamal leaving the club or another club buying him under these circumstances. That's a problem. I think we handled this very sensitively with the player, and we're all interested in him coming back - ideally in top form. But what happens if that's not the case? Then we'll still have to think about the finances. And that's a task that the board and the supervisory board unfortunately have to make.'.

Rummenigge added that he did not think it was 'problematic' for these discussions to be happening publicly, due to the club's interest in 'him coming back and playing well'.

But the player union Fifpro were forthright in their disagreement with his statements,  releasing a statement claiming that all parties currently sharing their views on Musiala's contract 'should know better'.

'Bayern's honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala's contract in quick succession,' the statement read.

'In Fifpro's view, this is a co-ordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern's standing should know better.'.

When this statement was shared to social media via journalist Fabrizio Romano, global talents including Jude Bellingham and Musiala's team-mate Michael Olise were among those to like the post.

Musiala collapsed on the pitch at two consecutive games in August (pictured being helped by team-mates against RB Leipzig).

The 23-year-old has been diagnosed with absence seizures and is managing his medication.

Vincent Kompany has been supportive of his player's struggles, and took him off the bench with some success last weekend.

Rio Ferdinand elaborated on those comments in a more detailed post on social media, adding that he believed the club are 'better than this'.

'If they want to negotiate more reasonable terms for the club going forward due to the health concerns Jamal has, then surely speak to him and his team rather than to the media,' Ferdinand wrote on X. 'This situation must be hard enough to deal with for Jamal without the media and club officials talking about it publicly.

Recent findings suggest that 'Bayern Munich are one of the clubs who from afar have always carried themselves with a class and standard that most have admired. Sadly, this just doesn't feel like Bayern Munich in this situation.'.

Criticisms were even more fiery in Germany, with the vice president of Germany's player union Michael Franz accusing the club of harassment.

'What the Bayern Munich officials are doing, and I don't mean Kompany and (Max) Eberl (director of sport), who have behaved impeccably, seems despicable to me,' Franz shared in an interview with Sport1. 'There is even something about it that resembles harassment.'.

'A footballer's level of performance can be discussed publicly, but it is not right to talk about his illness and the salary he receives in such circumstances. We must not forget that Jamal Musiala has done everything in his power to come back.'.

'Money has become more vital than the person, and that is unacceptable.'.

Former Bayern captain Stefan Effenberg stressed how notable 'support and protection' from the club towards their players is, particularly for those in greater need like Musiala.

'We are talking about someone who is suffering from an illness. What I would have expected is for the club's senior officials to apologise,' Effenberg mentioned, adding that he thought that the communications from the club had been 'disastrous'.

Musiala collapsed twice within four days in mid-August, first during Bayern's match against Leipzig – shortly after scoring – and then against Heidenheim.

He then returned to the pitch in September, netting against Bodo/Glimt in Champions League action and Union Berlin shortly before the first international break.

After suffering a hamstring injury, Musiala then spent time away from the side before his return at the end of last week – a match which also saw Harry Kane suffer an ankle injury which will keep him out for over three months.

Fifpro's statement went on to add that Bayern must be careful with their player's mental wellbeing as well as his physical challenges.

'Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala,' the statement continued. 'Across professional football, uncertainty about a player's future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury.

It has been revealed that 'Making Musiala's health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives.

Sources indicate that 'Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise.'.
